task.description: TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-02 Step 3b) hard gate on REQ-159's test coverage.
acceptance_criteria: All 8 REQ-159 acceptance criteria have real runnable test coverage, verified independently
The reported telemetry-based no-Repo-call test confirmed present, correctly implemented (handler cleanup, genuine measurement), and would actually catch the described mutation
The design-doc addendum confirmed genuinely present
Test isolation confirmed, including telemetry handler cleanup and real-Postgres fixtures

result.summary: All 8 REQ-159 acceptance criteria map to real, runnable tests in test/letflow/engine/lua/platform_test.exs and test/letflow/engine/lua_number_marshalling_test.exs, verified by direct reading against docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-159 entry and by running the suite myself: `mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/platform_test.exs test/letflow/engine/lua_number_marshalling_test.exs` -> 65 passed. The telemetry-based no-Repo-call test ('no Repo.get/3 (no [:letflow, :repo, :query] telemetry event) fires for a same-tenant sibling id', platform_test.exs:677-712) is present, attaches via :telemetry.attach/4 with a unique {module, name, make_ref()} handler id, detaches via on_exit(fn -> :telemetry.detach(handler_id) end) so it cannot leak into later tests, and measures absence of the real [:letflow, :repo, :query] event (Ecto's default telemetry_prefix for Letflow.Repo, confirmed against config and against test/letflow/api/context_test.exs's pre-existing, passing use of the identical event name for the identical purpose -- the new test mirrors that idiom correctly, not superficially: same handler-id shape, same :counters accumulator, same on_exit detach). I independently re-verified the discriminating power of this test rather than trusting the report: I applied the described mutation myself directly to lib/letflow/engine/lua/platform.ex (do_get_instance_state calling fetch_instance_state/Repo unconditionally first, then deciding forbidden/not_found/success after the fact), ran the suite, and got 56/57 passed with the sole failure being exactly the new telemetry test (assert :counters.get(counter,1)==0, left: 1, right: 0) -- matching TEST-DESIGNER's claimed numbers exactly. I then reverted via `git checkout -- lib/letflow/engine/lua/platform.ex`, confirmed `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` was empty, and re-ran the suite: 65 passed again, clean. The design-doc addendum is genuinely present in lib/letflow/design/req159-lua-host-api-read.md: two 'Post-implementation cross-reference note' sections (end of §6.4 and end of §7.4) document run_stub/3 becoming run_stub/5 (three prior args + execution_context + the call's own Lua.t()) rather than the originally-specified run_stub/4, and log's do_log/3 calling Lua.decode!/2 on the context argument explicitly before it reaches Logger.log/3's metadata -- both addenda match what is actually shipped in lib/letflow/engine/lua/platform.ex (arity-2 Lua.set!/3 wrapper fn args, call_lua -> ..., run_stub/5 clauses, and decode_log_context/2 calling Lua.decode!/2). No TODO/@tag :skip markers found in either test file or the spec. Test isolation confirmed: telemetry handler cleanup as above; real-Postgres fixtures (provisioned_tenant/0) each provision their own tenant with a freshly-generated id and drop the schema plus delete tenants/registrations rows in on_exit, unconditionally; every seed_projection! call uses a locally-generated instance_id, no shared/reused fixture state; module is async: false, ruling out interleaving on the process-global Sandbox.mode(:auto) call. No hardcoded secrets found (grepped for password/secret/api_key/SECRET across both test files and the spec -- no hits).
